subject: PioneerTrust RFI — exportability, retention windows, and tamper evidence
messages:
From: Samantha Reyes <samantha.reyes@pioneertrust.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@pioneertrust.com
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFI on audit exports, retention & integrity proofing

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks for agreeing to respond to the security & compliance section of our vendor RFP. Our procurement team attached the formal RFI (see attachment: PioneerTrust_RFP_section_AuditLogs.pdf) but I wanted to surface a few priority clarifications up front so our InfoSec team can triage. Could you confirm the following at a high level and we'll incorporate into the RFP table: 

1) Retention model — do you support time-based retention per tenant and per-route (e.g., chat logs 30 days, audit trail 7 years)? Are retention rules enforced server-side or client-managed?

2) Exportability — can we request bulk exports (full event history) and incremental/cursored exports (resume tokens) for a given time range? What formats do you support (ndjson, Parquet, CSV)?

3) Tamper evidence — do exported bundles include cryptographic manifests or signatures that allow us to verify immutability and chain-of-custody? If yes, which algorithms and what is included in the manifest?

4) Delivery options — S3 presigned, direct SFTP, or managed push to customer bucket with KMS encryption? Any constraints on export sizes or retention of export artifacts on Redwood side?

5) SLA & timelines — typical lead times for a full audit export (e.g., 6 months of logs) and guarantees around integrity during transit.

If you can answer these five items briefly we can mark them in the RFP matrix and then follow with a technical deep-dive. We're aiming to close this portion of the RFP by Jan 22.

Thanks — Samantha
Samantha Reyes
Senior Procurement Manager
PioneerTrust Bank

Attachments: PioneerTrust_RFP_section_AuditLogs.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Reyes <samantha.reyes@pioneertrust.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, procurement@pioneertrust.com
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFI on audit exports, retention & integrity proofing

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear set of questions. Attached is our formal RFI response (redwood_rfi_response_pioneertrust_20270110.pdf) which maps to the RFP table and includes example manifests and delivery options. Quick answers to your five bullets to expedite review: 

1) Retention model: Redwood supports tenant-scoped retention policies that can be configured per-route. Policies are enforced server-side in the control plane; we support time-based TTLs, legal-hold tags, and policy inheritance. Typical enforcement is immediate (delete/expiry job) with audit entries generated for retention actions.

2) Exportability: We support both bulk exports (time-range full harvest) and cursored/incremental exports (resume tokens for large windows). Supported output formats: ndjson (primary), Parquet (columnar), and gzipped CSV for CSV-based workflows. Exports are chunked for large windows and delivered with a manifest that lists chunks and byte ranges.

3) Tamper evidence: Export bundles include a SHA-256 manifest and an optional signed envelope using RSA-2048 or ECDSA-P256 (customer may request signing with Redwood-managed key or supply their own public key/KMS for signature verification). Manifest fields: chunk checksums, sequence IDs, timestamps, retention policy id, and a root manifest hash (SHA-256) for end-to-end verification. We also record an immutable ledger entry for export issuance (timestamped, append-only) retained per your retention contract.

4) Delivery options: Supported delivery: (a) Push to customer S3 bucket with SSE-KMS, (b) Presigned S3 objects, (c) Managed SFTP drop, (d) Secure HTTP POST to customer endpoint. We cap single export chunk at 50 GB; large exports are sharded and delivered as multipart chunks. Redwood retains export artifacts for 30 days by default (configurable in enterprise contracts) unless a longer staging window is requested.

5) SLA & timelines: Typical full export throughput depends on retention window and event volume; for planning we provide throughput estimates and hardened export jobs. Example: 6 months of medium-volume audit logs (approx 500M events) done via chunked export and parallel workers completes within 48–72 hours. We provide MD5/SHA-256 checksums per chunk and a signed manifest to guarantee integrity. Delivery confirmation and PoD (proof-of-delivery) is available via signed manifest receipt.

I'll follow up with a short sample manifest and S3 instructions. Happy to schedule a technical deep-dive with our security engineering team next week.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Product Manager, Security Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_rfi_response_pioneertrust_20270110.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Tim Hsieh <tim.hsieh@auditec.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Reyes <samantha.reyes@pioneertrust.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 08:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Follow-up: manifest contents and root-hash verification

Hi Karthik — I'm Tim from Auditec; PioneerTrust engaged us to validate integrity claims for vendor exports. Two quick clarifications after a preliminary read of your PDF: 

• When you say "root manifest hash (SHA-256)" — is that an over-arching Merkle root across chunks or a simple concatenated-hash approach? We need to understand the verification steps to include in our audit plan.

• For key management, does Redwood support customer-supplied public keys for signatures (we prefer customer-supplied keys and not Redwood KMS for proof)? If so, what's the onboarding flow (format, TTL of acceptance, rotation)?

• Can you provide a redacted sample manifest for a 30-day export and a small test payload we can use to run verification tooling (we don't need full logs, just schema + example chunks + checksums)?

Thanks — Tim
Lead Engineer, Integrity Services
Auditec Labs

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Hsieh <tim.hsieh@auditec.com>, Samantha Reyes <samantha.reyes@pioneertrust.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 15:43:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: manifest contents and root-hash verification

Hi Tim / Samantha — Laura here from Security & Compliance. Appreciate the close read — answers inline: 

• Root manifest hash: We currently implement a Merkle-tree style root over chunk-level SHA-256 digests for strong tamper resistance. Each chunk has a SHA-256 checksum; we compute an ordered Merkle root and publish the root in the root manifest and the ledger entry. Verification steps for your tooling: (1) verify each chunk SHA-256 against the manifest, (2) recompute the Merkle root from the chunk digests in the same ordering (we also include ordering metadata), (3) validate the signature on the manifest. We've included a small sample manifest (audit_export_sample_manifest.json) in this thread — it's redacted and includes chunk digests, sizes, offsets, sequence IDs, retention policy id, and the merkle root.

• Customer-supplied keys: yes — we support onboarding customer public keys (PEM format) for manifest signing. Onboarding flow: deliver PEM via our secure key exchange portal (or SFTP) with an onboarding ticket; we pin the public key to the tenant id and include the key fingerprint in the manifest. Key TTL/rotation: standard lifecycle supports rotation (you can provide rotation schedule); Redwood stores only the public key and a rotation history (no private key). We can also support short TTL signing tokens if you require ephemeral verification keys.

• Test payload & validation: attached is audit_export_sample_manifest.json and a small gzipped chunk sample. You can run the standard verification: check chunk checksum, recompute merkle root, then verify ECDSA-P256 signature using the onboarded public key. If you'd like we can run a joint test where we push a small 7-day export to a PioneerTrust test S3 bucket and provide a pre-signed URL for verification.

Next steps:
- We'll provision a sample export and push instructions to your test bucket if you confirm the target S3 bucket details (bucket name, preferred KMS key ARN).
- Propose a 60-minute technical validation call next Tuesday (Jan 19) with our Security Eng and the Auditec team. Please let us know preferred times.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: audit_export_sample_manifest.json (application/json), s3_delivery_instructions.txt (text/plain)
